{"lessons": ["

Forming the imperfetto

This is the most regular tense in Italian. Drop the -re and add -vo, -vi, -va, -vamo, -vate, -vano.

parlareprenderedormire
ioparlavoprendevodormivo
tuparlaviprendevidormivi
lui/leiparlavaprendevadormiva
noiparlavamoprendevamodormivamo
voiparlavateprendevatedormivate
loroparlavanoprendevanodormivano

Only four irregulars: essere (ero, eri, era, eravamo, eravate, erano), fare (facevo), dire (dicevo), bere (bevevo).

Pronunciation: the stress falls on the a in “parlavano”, not on the ending.

", "

Which one to choose?

English often uses the simple past for both (“I went”), so this takes a little practice. A good guide: if English could say “was …ing” or “used to”, or if you're setting the scene, it's the imperfetto; if it's one completed event (“I did”), it's the passato prossimo.

ImperfettoPassato prossimo
background, descriptionspecific event
past habit (“used to”)finished action, with a time
action in progress (“was …ing”)the action that interrupts it
Mentre aspettavo il treno, è arrivato Paolo.While I was waiting for the train, Paolo arrived.
Da bambino andavo al mare ogni estate.As a child, I used to go to the beach every summer.

Two nuances to know

Ho conosciuto = I met (for the first time). Ho saputo = I found out (a piece of news).

To stress that an action was in progress: stare in the imperfetto + gerund, just like English “was + -ing”. “Stavo mangiando” = I was eating.
